name: Ohio Court of Claims — Public Records Complaints
covers: Formal complaints when a public office denies a records request or fails to respond. This is the cheap, fast alternative to a mandamus action.
account_notes: File online with a credit card, by mail with a check or money order payable to the Ohio Court of Claims, or in person with cash.
submission_notes: A special master is appointed and mediation is offered. Final orders may be appealed to the court of appeals for the district where the public office has its principal place of business (R.C. 2743.75(G)(1)).
notes: VERIFIED 2026-08-11 — $25 non-refundable fee and appellate-district rule confirmed against the court's own page and codes.ohio.gov.

name: Ohio Revised Code (codes.ohio.gov)
covers: Primary text of the Ohio Public Records Act and every other statute you will cite. Always quote from here, never from a summary.
submission_notes: Section 149.43 is the Public Records Act. Section 2743.75 is the Court of Claims complaint process.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-08-11 — statute sets NO fixed day count: inspection 'promptly', copies 'within a reasonable period of time'.

name: Ohio Attorney General — Sunshine Laws / Yellow Book
covers: The AG's annual Sunshine Laws manual — the standard reference public offices themselves are trained on. Quote it back to them.
submission_notes: Cite the current edition by year and page when disputing a denial.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-08-11 — page resolved. Confirm the current-year edition before citing a page number.

name: Supreme Court of Ohio — Opinions & Case Search
covers: Ohio Supreme Court opinions and dockets. Where you find the controlling public-records case law.
submission_notes: Search by docket number, case title, or full text.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-08-11 via search.

name: Ohio Auditor of State — Audit Search
covers: Released audit reports for ~5,000 units of Ohio government, including Findings for Recovery (public money not handled according to law).
submission_notes: Findings for Recovery are the highest-value item here. Search by entity and year.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-08-11 via search.

name: Ohio Secretary of State — Business Entity Search
covers: Every registered LLC, corporation, partnership, trade name and trademark in Ohio, with filed images. Core due-diligence lookup.
submission_notes: Free, no registration. Pull the actual filing images, not just the summary screen — officers and agents are on the images.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-08-11 via search.

name: Franklin County Clerk of Courts — Case Information Online (CIO)
covers: Common Pleas civil and criminal, Domestic Relations, and 10th District Court of Appeals cases.
typical_fees: free to search; copy fees apply
submission_notes: Search by party name or case number. You must accept a disclaimer page first. Phone: 614-525-3600.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-08-11 via search.

name: Franklin County Municipal Court Clerk — Case Search
covers: Municipal court cases: misdemeanors, traffic, evictions, small claims. This is where most local police charges land.
submission_notes: Search by case or ticket number for best results; name search also works.
notes: VERIFIED 2026-08-11 via search. RELEVANT: municipal-level criminal cases in Franklin County appear here.

name: Columbus City Council — Legistar
covers: Full ordinance, resolution, agenda and minutes history for Columbus City Council. Where ordinances like 3142-2023 and 1075-2024 live.
submission_notes: Search by ordinance number or keyword; export result lists. Attachments hold the contracts.
notes: NOT CONFIRMED THIS SESSION — run scripts/check_portals.js to verify before relying on it.

name: City of Columbus — Public Records Request
covers: Central intake for City of Columbus records requests, including Department of Public Utilities.
submission_notes: Route DPU rate and consent-order questions here and ask them to confirm the custodian in writing.
notes: VERIFY the exact records-request landing URL — city sites reorganize often.

name: Franklin County Auditor — Property Search
covers: Parcel ownership, valuation, transfers, and tax history. Primary tool for property due diligence.
submission_notes: Search by address, owner, or parcel ID. Transfer history shows the chain of ownership.
notes: VERIFY URL before first use.

name: Franklin County Recorder — Official Records Search
covers: Deeds, mortgages, liens, easements, UCC filings. Where you prove who actually owns and who is owed.
submission_notes: Search by name or instrument number. Certified copies cost extra.
notes: VERIFY URL before first use.

name: City of Gahanna — Public Records Request
covers: City of Gahanna records intake, including police department reports, body-worn camera footage, and dispatch/CAD records.
submission_notes: Body-worn camera requests are their own category under R.C. 149.43(A)(17) restricted-portion rules — ask for the unredacted-to-you portions and get any withholding cited in writing.
notes: VERIFY the exact records-request URL and the records custodian's title before filing.

name: City of Reynoldsburg — Public Records Request
covers: Reynoldsburg records intake — water/wastewater billing, council, service department.
submission_notes: Email publicrecords@reynoldsburg.gov. Carried over from your v0.5 seed set.

name: Ohio EPA — eDocument Search
covers: Ohio EPA permits, findings and orders, and correspondence. Where consent orders and Director's Final Findings & Orders are filed.
submission_notes: Search by facility or document type. Director's Final Findings & Orders are the primary documents behind the consent-order language in the sewer ordinances.
notes: VERIFY URL. If the portal search fails, file a records request with Ohio EPA's records office instead.

name: Ohio Water Development Authority
covers: OWDA loan applications, board minutes, and the state loan portfolio for water/sewer projects.
submission_notes: Board minutes are posted; the full loan portfolio usually requires a records request.
notes: VERIFY URL before first use.

name: Ohio Secretary of State — Campaign Finance
covers: Contribution and expenditure filings for state candidates, PACs, and committees. Follow the money into the decision.
submission_notes: County boards of elections hold local candidate filings that never reach the state system — request those separately.
notes: VERIFY URL. Local races are usually at the county board of elections, not here.

name: Ohio Ethics Commission — Financial Disclosure
covers: Annual financial disclosure statements for Ohio public officials. Shows outside income, creditors, and conflicts.
submission_notes: Statements are generally obtainable on request; the requester's identity may be disclosed to the filer in some circumstances — confirm before filing.
notes: IMPORTANT: verify the notification rule before requesting. This is one of the few Ohio contexts where anonymity may not hold.

name: PACER — Federal Court Records
covers: All federal district, bankruptcy, and appellate dockets and filings.
account_notes: Free registration required. Provide billing details at signup; fees are waived below the quarterly threshold.
typical_fees: $0.10 per page, $3.00 cap per document; fees waived if quarterly usage stays under the threshold
submission_notes: Use the free CourtListener/RECAP mirror first to avoid paying for documents someone already pulled.
notes: VERIFY current fee schedule and threshold — these change.

name: CourtListener / RECAP Archive
covers: Free mirror of federal court documents already pulled from PACER, plus state appellate opinions.
submission_notes: Always check here before spending PACER money.
notes: VERIFY URL before first use.

name: USAspending.gov
covers: Federal contracts, grants, and loans by recipient. Good for tracing federal money into local projects.
submission_notes: Search by recipient name and by place of performance.
notes: VERIFY URL before first use.

name: SAM.gov — Entity & Exclusions Search
covers: Federal contractor registration and the exclusions (debarment) list. Check every contractor here.
submission_notes: The exclusions list is the fast red-flag check in any vendor due-diligence pass.
notes: VERIFY URL before first use.

name: Columbus Metropolitan Library — Public Records Request
covers: Columbus Metropolitan Library system records: board minutes, budgets, policies, contracts, branch records.
submission_notes: CML is its own public office with its own records custodian. Do NOT route library requests through the City of Columbus — the city is not the custodian and the request will die there.
notes: VERIFY the records-request contact and custodian title before filing. Added 2026-08-11 after a bad auto-link routed a CML branch to the City of Columbus.

name: FEC — Campaign Finance Data
covers: Federal candidate, committee and PAC filings: who gave, to whom, how much. Free API at api.open.fec.gov with a key from api.data.gov.
submission_notes: The API is the fast path — see modules/connectors (fec). Individual contributions are schedule_a; independent expenditures are schedule_e.
notes: VERIFY URL. Federal only — Ohio state and local candidates are NOT here.

name: U.S. Senate — Lobbying Disclosure
covers: Quarterly federal lobbying filings: which firm is paid by which client, how much, and on which bills. Free API, optional key.
submission_notes: Registrant is the lobbying firm; client is who pays. The issue codes tell you the subject matter. Cross-reference against FEC for the same client.
notes: VERIFY URL. Covers FEDERAL lobbying only. Ohio has a separate JLEC registry.

name: Ohio Joint Legislative Ethics Committee — Lobbying
covers: Ohio legislative and executive agency lobbyist registrations and expenditure reports. The state-level counterpart to the Senate LDA.
submission_notes: This is where Ohio Statehouse lobbying lives. No public API — search the web portal and file a records request for bulk data.
notes: VERIFY URL. CRITICAL for Ohio state politics — federal LDA does NOT cover the Statehouse.

name: County Board of Elections — Local Campaign Finance
covers: LOCAL candidate and issue-committee campaign finance filings: county commissioners, city council, school board, township trustees, levy committees.
submission_notes: THE gap in every API. Local candidate filings never reach the Ohio SOS system and are not in FEC. You must go to the county BOE directly — in person or by records request. One BOE per county.
notes: VERIFY each county BOE URL separately. This row is a REMINDER of the method, not a single portal.

name: Ohio Checkbook — State Expenditures
covers: State of Ohio spending by vendor, agency and category. Local governments participate voluntarily, so coverage below the state level is uneven.
submission_notes: Good for tracing a vendor across state agencies. Absence here does NOT mean absence of payment — check the entity's own records too.
notes: VERIFY URL and confirm which of your seven counties participate.
